entrypoint_protocol: Invoke with argv as `python3 todo.py [--data-file PATH] <command> [arguments]`. Commands are `add TITLE`, `list [--all]`, `done ID`, and `stats`. Normal output is written to stdout, diagnostic errors to stderr, and invalid usage or operations return exit code 2.
objective: Build a robust multi-file argv todo CLI with persistent local JSON state, add/list/done/stats commands, helpful errors, and real automated tests.
public_behavior_spec: `python3 todo.py --help` exits 0 and documents the add, list, done, and stats commands.
`add TITLE` rejects an absent or whitespace-only title; otherwise it creates a pending todo with a stable positive integer ID, persists it, exits 0, and prints `Added todo ID: TITLE`.
`list` shows pending todos in ascending ID order as `[ ] ID: TITLE`; when no pending todos exist it prints `No pending todos.`.
`list --all` shows both pending and completed todos in ascending ID order, using `[ ] ID: TITLE` for pending items and `[x] ID: TITLE` for completed items.
`done ID` marks an existing pending todo complete, persists the change, exits 0, and prints `Completed todo ID: TITLE`.
`done` rejects malformed, unknown, or already-completed IDs with exit code 2 and a concise diagnostic on stderr.
`stats` prints separate `Total: N`, `Pending: N`, and `Completed: N` lines whose counts reflect persisted state.
`--data-file PATH` selects the JSON state file, allowing isolated stores. A missing file represents an empty store, and successful mutations create parent directories when needed.
State is valid UTF-8 JSON and remains readable across separate process invocations. Writes avoid leaving a partially written state file.
Unknown commands, invalid options, malformed state, and filesystem failures terminate without a traceback, return a nonzero exit code, and provide a helpful diagnostic.
The implementation is split across the top-level launcher and importable modules under `todo_cli`.
The repository includes automated tests under `tests` that exercise the CLI using isolated temporary state files and require no network service.

public_tests.description: The argv entrypoint exposes help for every required command.
A previously absent state file behaves as an empty todo store.
Adds, completion state, filtering, and statistics survive separate process invocations against one JSON file.
Completing an ID that is not present is rejected with the documented error exit status.
Whitespace-only todo titles are rejected rather than persisted.
An unsupported command produces a usage error.
The required multi-file implementation modules import without launching the CLI or failing.
public_tests.script:
import todo_cli.cli
import todo_cli.storage
print('imports ok')

public_tests.description: The submitted automated tests execute successfully with the Python standard-library test runner.

qualitative_rubric: Core command behavior is demonstrated by successful execution of add, list, done, and stats through the public argv entrypoint.
Persistence is demonstrated across independent processes using the same selected JSON file.
Failure cases return stable nonzero statuses without corrupting previously valid state.
The implementation separates command parsing, storage concerns, and the launcher into the required importable files.
Automated tests execute real subprocess behavior, isolate their state with temporary paths, and cover successful operations plus representative failures.
The solution uses only local resources and remains portable on a standard Python 3 installation.
stopping_condition: Stop when all required artifacts exist, every public executable test passes from a clean workspace, and the manager determines whether the result is eligible for release.
